9. He further submits that from the medical evidence it will appear that the victim died on a road accident and admittedly at that time she was not in the custody of the appellant as such onus does not lie upon him to prove how the victim met her death. 

 11. He further submits that since Nasir, who has alleged to call the victim from the house of the informant and Fazlu, to whose shop victim was alleged to visit in the date of occurrence to meet her husband, were not examined in court, the appellant is entitled to get benefit under section 114(G) of the Evidence Act. 

 12. He further submits that in this case there is no eye-witness but the trial court although found there is no continuity in the chain of circumstances, even then convicted the appellant upon relying that uncorroborated circumstantial evidence. Impugned conviction is thus not sustainable in law which is liable to be set aside. He lastly submits that since the impugned conviction was passed on mere surmises and conjecture, the appellant is entitled to get the order of acquittal. Learned advocate relied some decision in support of his submissions Viz. Zahirul Islam @ Dipu (Md) vs State reported in 20 BLC (AD) 129, Habibur Rahman @ Habu vs State reported in 18 BLC (AD) 218, Habez Md Piru Kazi vs State reported in BCR 2004 HCD 90, State vs Khasru Syed Mostafa Hossain reported in 43 DLR (AD) 182, State vs Monu Miah reported in 54 DLR (AD) 60. 

 13. Mr SM Shahjahan the learned advocate also appearing for the appellant, conceding the above submission further argued that this is absolutely a case of no evidence and the appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt and may be acquitted. 

 14. The learned Deputy Attorney General Mr Md Bashir Ullah assisted by Mr AKM Shafiqul Islam advocate appearing for the state submits that; by the evidence of PW6 Md Saidur Rahman (Paltu), PW7 Md Shamim Al Mamun, PW10 Advocate Md Hafizur Rahman and PW11 Shahidur Rahman, the prosecution has successfully able to prove that the victim was seen lastly on the date of occurrence with the accused appellant and thereafter she found missing and her dead body was recovered from the place of occurrence and, as such, the trial court committed no illegality in convicting the appellant, upon considering this circumstantial evidence as the last seen theory. The appeal thus contains no merits which may be dismissed. In support of his contention he relied upon a decisions. viz. The State vs Rafiqul Islam reported in 4 SCOB (2015) HCD 139. 

 43. These are the evidences of the prosecution sides. 

 47. In view of the matter when the victim was found to be accompanied by her husband on the very date of occurrence and thereafter her dead body was found on the road side, death was obviously caused by the reason best known to her husband who was lastly been seen along with her. The defence case, to the effect-that victim met her death by a road accident are not been proved by any evidence either by putting any suggestion to the prosecution witnesses or by giving any defence witness. Be that as it may thus, it can easily be held that the prosecution version to the effect that victim was killed by the accused who was lastly been seen to be accompanied with her can only be held to be probable in the case to commit murder to the victim. The decisions cited in the instant case by the appellant get no reference to help the accused in any manner. We found that there is a clear link of chain on the circumstantial evidence that on the date of occurrence, victim went out of her house and been seen together with the accused in the chamber of PW6 lawyer Md Shamsur Rahman and thereafter her dead body was found to the place of occurrence. Accordingly when victim was found lastly accompanied by her husband, he is obviously liable to say how his wife met her death. But in the case, the accused husband could not bear that responsibilities rather the alive taken by him to the effect that victim died on road accident is not been proved by any evidence, clearly established that there is none but by him who is responsible for killing his wife by taking any means best known to him. Moreover after the date of occurrence accused found absconding without taking his responsibilities to prove his innocence or help to the prosecution to find out the real killer of his wife which is also proved about his guilty mind. The trial court thus committed no illegality to award conviction to the appellant.
